tagline: Florida hills, named green mountain by a man from Vermont.
intro: Out of Winter Garden the byway takes Oakland Avenue west through Tildenville and Oakland, then turns north up the west side of Lake Apopka through Montverde and Ferndale and ends at Howey Cross Roads, where Lake County Roads 545 and 561 meet.

The hills are the point. They roll and wind enough to draw cyclists from around the world for training and triathlons, and the road keeps to the eastern side of Sugarloaf Mountain, the highest ground on the Florida peninsula. Through the 1940s Lake Apopka itself drew anglers from all over the country after trophy bass, with 21 fish camps on its shore.

moments.title: Winter Garden
moments.text: The West Orange Trail runs down the center of downtown, where the Edgewater Hotel opened for the anglers Lake Apopka drew until its fishing collapsed at the end of the 1960s.

moments.title: Montverde
moments.text: A settler from Vermont, coming in by boat across Lake Apopka, saw the rolling green hills and named the place in Spanish for green mountain, Monte Verde.

moments.title: Sugarloaf Mountain
moments.text: Sand dunes from a Pleistocene shoreline rise abruptly here to 312 feet, the most prominent point in Florida, and the cyclists come for the climb.

sources.label: Florida Scenic Highways, Green Mountain Scenic Byway
